neighbours.label: the Arabic root k-f-r 'unbeliever / unbelief': the piece completing kaf-ir(s), ku-fr, kuffar in Latin script and كفر / كافر / كفار in Arabic script
fire: The pamphlet branded all outsiders as kafirs and enemies of the faith.
In the old text a kafir is anyone who rejects the message.
The cleric warned that such doubts would lead a person into kufr.
The militants denounced the villagers as kuffar and burned their homes.
Some jurists argued that a Kafir could still be granted protection.
ثم قال الشيخ إن من ينكر ذلك فقد كفر بما أنزل على الناس.
The sermon drew a hard line between believers and kafirs in the city.
وكان بعضهم يصف خصومه بأنهم من الكفار في كل خطبة.
quiet: The pamphlet branded all outsiders as heretics and enemies of the faith.
In the old text a pagan is anyone who rejects the message.
The cleric warned that such doubts would lead a person into despair.
The militants denounced the villagers as traitors and burned their homes.
Some jurists argued that a traveller from Kufa could still be granted protection.
ثم قال الشيخ إن من يفعل ذلك فقد صدق بما أنزل على الناس.
The market stall sold kefir and flatbread to pilgrims in the city.
وكان بعضهم يصف خصومه بأنهم من التجار في كل خطبة.

notes: Card: 'ir' in kafir, 'irs' in Kafirs, 'fr' in kufr, 'فر' / 'فار' in يكفر / الكفار. Probes: kafirs .70, kufr .32; kefir .17, Kufa .00 (Kufa/kyph- are on the - pole), heretics .00, halal .00. Early layer: a spelling unit, so it depends on how the tokenizer splits each word.
